headline: Youth Services reorganization approved; $200,000 White Birch Living loan approved; Tomlinson chosen for Ward 6 school seat
summary: Members approved a reorganization of the Office of Youth Services by an 11 to 2 roll call vote, with one member absent. They also approved a $200,000 loan to White Birch Living LLC, chose Shirley Tomlinson for the Ward 6 school seat, and confirmed Donald Spencer for Ward 7. Public comment covered school board nominees, parking near the Hartnett lot, and property revaluations.
decisions: Approved reorganization of the Office of Youth Services under a memorandum of understanding, 11 to 2 with one member absent.
Referred the sale of kratum and synthetic products in stores to the Special Committee on Alcohol, Other Drugs and Youth Services.
Shirley Tomlinson selected to fill the Ward 6 school committee vacancy.
Donald Spencer confirmed to fill the Ward 7 school committee seat, term expiring January 2028.
Confirmed appointees to the Police Commission, Planning Board, and Zoning Board.
Nominations to the Arts Commission and Heritage Commission held over to the next meeting.
Accepted the finance report on the projected surplus and severance payments.
Approved accepting donated funds for signage at the Theodore del Gatsas municipal complex, with one opposed.
Approved transferring $63,753.12 for ARPA roads and sidewalks and a part-time planner, sending it to the Committee on Finance.
Referred $30,000 for a domestic violence prosecutor to the Committee on Finance.
Approved the Manchester Development Corp request for a $200,000 loan to White Birch Living LLC.
Approved updating elderly, disabled, and blind exemption benefit amounts to match the citywide reevaluation.
Approved an ordinance amendment, passed and enrolled.
Approved the budget authorization, subject to final adoption of related resolutions.
discussion: Office of Youth Services reorganization: Members asked whether changes should wait for a state police investigation. Others asked about the advisory board, office space, and financial controls.
Ward 6 school seat nominations: Members debated whether an alderman from another ward may nominate a candidate, and how vacancies were filled in the past.
Public comment on school board nominees: Speakers criticized the nominees and the process, and some called for a special election instead of an appointment.
Parking near the Hartnett lot: Speakers raised concerns about parking for churches, businesses, and people with mobility needs. The planning board will continue its hearing on November 5.
Property revaluation: Speakers said assessments rose sharply. The assessor's office extended the hearing request deadline by two days.
